answer.text:
The September 2024 master-data assessment (Kwame Boateng's email of 30 September 2024) reported the remediation scope for the pilot cohort with these figures: 4,214 articles in the cohort, 1,317 missing case pack quantity, 3,105 missing or default supplier lead time, and shelf life populated on 48%. It stated case pack is the blocker, lead times can be worked around by deriving actuals from receipt history, and shelf life is out of scope for that phase. The attached file with the 1,317 articles is not available in the supplied evidence. [1]

The 24 September 2024 master-data workshop had already quantified case pack quantity as missing on thirty-one percent of active articles (Kwame Boateng, completing a sentence begun across turns with Priya Nair). The workshop also noted store master is clean and the product hierarchy was being discussed, but no completion status for remediation was reported at that point. [2] [3] [4] [5] [6]

The underlying assessment findings date from May 2024 (Tomas Lindholm's write-up of 2 May 2024): ECC 6.0 is fine with no concerns about the nightly batch for daily replenishment; DC-2 goes in as a named risk (out-of-support middleware, intermittent failure, silent mode); master data needs a remediation workstream owned on the client side, with case pack quantity the blocking gap; and remaining shelf life obtainability was an open question. Priya Nair agreed on all four and said she would own the remediation (6 May 2024). [7] [8]

Distinguishing assessment from remediation completion: nothing in September 2024 reports any remediation as complete. The case pack remediation was completed later, on 19 December 2024, when Priya Nair reported "Done. All 1,317", with the two unresponsive suppliers resolved by measuring actual delivered quantities over six months and inferring the case pack, right for 190 of the 200 articles. Ana Duarte recorded it in the steering report on 20 December 2024 and noted shelf life remains at 48% and untouched, correct for that phase and becoming the critical path for phase two. At the 21 January 2025 UAT readiness review, Priya Nair confirmed case pack for the cohort is done (about thirteen hundred articles, finished 19 December) and that lead times she has not touched, still mostly sevens. [9] [10] [11] [12] [13]

So the September 2024 assessment reported scope figures and priorities, not completions: 4,214 cohort articles, 1,317 missing case pack, 3,105 missing or default lead times, 48% shelf life populated. The only item later reported complete was case pack (1,317 articles, 19 December 2024); lead times were never remediated (derived from receipt history instead per the assessment workaround) and shelf life remained at 48%, explicitly out of scope for that phase. [1] [9] [10] [12] [13]

Assessment written up as promised. Four conclusions.

ECC 6.0 is fine and we have no concerns about the nightly batch for daily replenishment.
